question.text: The slope at any point of a curve $y=f(x)$ is given by $\frac{d y}{d x}=3 x^2$ and it passes through $(-1,1)$. The equation of the curve is

solution.text:
Hints: $\frac{d y}{d x}=3 x^2 \Rightarrow \int d y=\int 3 x^2 d x \Rightarrow y=x^3+\mathrm{C}$
Curve passes through $(-1,1)$. Hence $1=-1+C \Rightarrow C=2$
$$
\therefore y=x^3+2
$$
